q1857: Article 352 deals with a Proclamation of (National) Emergency; Article 356 with President's Rule in states and Article 360 with Financial Emergency.

Other Indian tennis names: Leander Paes, Rohan Bopanna, Sumit Nagal.
q1860: The Netherlands won the 2018 FIH Women's Hockey World Cup in London, beating Ireland in the final.
The Netherlands are the most successful women's hockey nation.

q1934: The Khazana Building Museum is near Golconda in Hyderabad, Telangana; it holds sculptures and inscriptions from the Kakatiya and other dynasties.
q1935: Tata vadya are string instruments (veena, chitra veena, santoor); the flute is a wind instrument (sushira vadya).
Natyashastra's four groups: tata (strings), sushira (wind), avanaddha (drums), ghana (solid).

Modhera Sun Temple was built by the Solankis.
q1937: Halda is a winter festival of the Lahaul valley in Himachal Pradesh, dedicated to the goddess of wealth, Shiskar Apa.

q1938: In a socialist (command) economy the government owns the means of production and decides what, how and for whom goods are produced, according to society's needs.

RBI started work on 1 April 1935 under the 1934 Act.
q1940: GNP minus depreciation gives Net National Product (NNP).
GNP − depreciation = NNP; NNP at factor cost = National Income.
q1941: The government budget is an annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure (Article 112), not of 'receipts and borrowing'; it has two parts, the revenue budget and the capital budget.
Revenue budget + capital budget = Union Budget.
q1942: Bank Rate is the rate at which the RBI buys or rediscounts bills of exchange (not sells them); it is now aligned to the Marginal Standing Facility rate. So only II is correct.
q1943: Spinach contains oxalic acid. Tamarind has tartaric acid, ant stings formic acid, curd lactic acid.

q1946: Larger amplitude gives a louder sound, and higher frequency gives a higher pitch, so both pairs are correct.
q1947: Soil forms from parent rock over time, shaped by climate, relief and living organisms.
Five factors: parent rock, climate, relief, organisms, time.
q1948: Cotton needs high temperature (21–30°C), light rainfall (50–100 cm), 210 frost-free days and bright sunshine; black soil suits it best.
Gujarat and Maharashtra lead in cotton.
q1949: From the ground up the atmosphere's layers are troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere (the third), thermosphere and exosphere.
q1950: India covers about 3.28 million sq km, roughly 2.4% of the world's land area, and is the seventh-largest country.
2.4% of land but about 17% of people.
q1951: The Purna is a tributary of the Godavari and the Bhima a tributary of the Krishna, so both pairs are correct.
Other Godavari tributaries: Pranhita, Indravati, Manjra; Krishna: Tungabhadra, Koyna.
q1952: About 8,000 years ago people in the Sulaiman and Kirthar hills (north-west) first grew wheat and barley and domesticated sheep and goats (NCERT). Rice is recorded first to the north of the Vindhyas.

q1953: Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at the Battle of Khanwa (Khanua) in 1527.

The World Bank's 'Business Ready' (B-READY) report replaced it.

q1965: Article 112 requires the President to lay the Annual Financial Statement (the Union Budget) before Parliament.
q1966: Article 248: Parliament has exclusive power over any matter not listed in the Concurrent or State List (residuary powers), including taxes not mentioned in either list.
Residuary powers lie with the Union (Canadian model).
q1967: The Eleventh Schedule (73rd Amendment) lists 29 subjects for panchayats, including fisheries and family welfare.
q1968: The Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium is in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.
Largest capacity in India: Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.
q1969: India won 24 silver medals at the 2018 Jakarta–Palembang Asian Games (15 gold, 24 silver, 30 bronze = 69).
q1970: Badminton and archery are both Summer Olympic sports and were contested at Tokyo 2020 (held in 2021).
P.V. Sindhu won bronze in badminton at Tokyo.
q1975: Kangra Fort, one of India's oldest forts, is in Himachal Pradesh. Golconda: Telangana; Warangal: Telangana; Kumbhalgarh: Rajasthan.
Kumbhalgarh has the second-longest continuous wall in the world.
q1976: Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala, with elaborate make-up and costumes and stories from the epics.

q1978: Khatarua (an autumn fire festival) and Phool Dei (a spring flower festival) are both festivals of Uttarakhand.

q1979: Real GDP values output at the prices of a fixed base year, removing the effect of price changes; nominal GDP uses current prices.
q1980: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 divided industries into three schedules and gave the public sector the leading role; it followed the first IPR of 1948.
q1981: In a closed economy demand for domestic goods comes from consumption, investment and government spending; net exports exist only in an open economy.
Closed: C + I + G; open: C + I + G + (X − M).
q1982: Both statements about depreciation are correct: it is an annual allowance for wear and tear, and in simple accounting it is the cost of the good divided by its years of useful life. So neither is incorrect.
q1983: Both statements are correct: in open market operations the RBI buys or sells government securities to change the stock of high-powered money, and when it buys a bond it pays by cheque, creating new money. So neither is incorrect.
RBI buys securities → money supply rises.
q1984: Bile is made by the liver and stored in the gall bladder; it emulsifies fats in the small intestine.
Bile has no enzymes, only bile salts.
q1985: Radioactive iodine (I-131), not uranium, treats goitre and thyroid disorders; cobalt-60 is used in cancer radiotherapy. So only II is correct.
Iodine → thyroid; cobalt → cancer; carbon-14 → dating.
q1986: Fertilisation happens in sexual reproduction, and spore formation is asexual, so both pairs are wrong.
q1987: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, smaller image, including for an object at infinity; a concave mirror forms a same-size image at C when the object is at C. Both pairs are correct.
Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors.
q1988: Asia produces more than half of the world's tin; China, Malaysia and Indonesia are leading producers (NCERT).
Tin is used for tinplating and solder.
q1989: India's land boundary is about 15,200 km long; its coastline (with islands) is about 7,516 km.
q1990: The Northern Plains stretch about 2,400 km from east to west and are 240–320 km wide, formed by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra systems.
q1991: The stratosphere lies above the troposphere and reaches up to about 50 km; it contains the ozone layer and is good for jet flights.
Troposphere to about 13 km; stratosphere to about 50 km.

Jinnah announced it after the Cabinet Mission plan failed.

It was first published free online during the COVID-19 lockdown.
q1999: NATO (formed 1949) is headquartered in Brussels, Belgium.
EU institutions are also in Brussels.

No money leaves the Consolidated Fund without an Appropriation Act.

Civil proceedings need two months' notice.

q2021: Sattriya, founded by the saint Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th–16th century, originated in the sattras (monasteries) of Assam; it was recognised as a classical dance in 2000.

Monopoly: one seller; oligopoly: a few.
q2025: Capital goods are durable goods used in production over many years, such as machines, tools and buildings; consumption goods satisfy wants directly.
q2026: GNP = GDP + Net factor income from abroad.
